citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $R>0$, let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$,
let $k>0$ and $d\in S^2$. On $\mathcal H=L^2(B_R;\mathbb C)$ let
$K_kf(x)=\int_{B_R}G_k(x-y)V(y)f(y)dy$, where
$G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$. The supplier
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-outgoing-fredholm-invertibility]] supplies
bounded invertibility of $I+K_k$. Define

$$u=(I+K_k)^{-1}(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_R}),\qquad \Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_R}G_k(x-y)V(y)u(y)dy,\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}.$$

Then:

(a) $\Psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$,
$(-\Delta+V-k^2)\Psi=0$ distributionally, and $\Psi|_{B_R}=u$.

(b) With $r=|x|>2R$, $\Omega=x/r$, the smooth amplitude

$$f_k(\Omega)=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_{B_R}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}V(y)u(y)dy$$

satisfies $\Psi=e^{ikd\cdot x}+e^{ikr}f_k(\Omega)/r+\mathcal E(r,\Omega)$.
The error and its first radial derivative are bounded uniformly in $\Omega$
by $C(k,R,\|Vu\|_1)r^{-2}$. For every fixed finite product $D_\Omega$ of
smooth tangential differential operators on $S^2$, also
$|D_\Omega\mathcal E|+|D_\Omega\partial_r\mathcal E|\le C_Dr^{-2}$.

(c) Fix normalization constants $\hbar,m>0$. The scattered radial current is

$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=\frac\hbar m\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}}\,\partial_r\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}})=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),$$

uniformly in $\Omega$. With incident plane-wave flux density
$J_{\mathrm{in}}=\hbar k/m$, the stationary elastic model's differential
cross section is

$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}=\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)}{J_{\mathrm{in}}}=|f_k(\Omega)|^2,\qquad \sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\sigma<\infty.$$

These are conditional model statements. Measured count rates additionally
require incident fluence, target and detector acceptance, efficiency and
background modelling; none is asserted. Part (a) is a local regularity
statement for a stationary scattering wave, with no assertion of membership
in the global $L^2$ operator domain.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $R>0$, let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with $\operatorname{supp}V\subseteq B_R$,
and put $\mathcal H=L^2(B_R;\mathbb C)$. For $k>0$ define

$$K_kf(x)=\int_{B_R}\frac{e^{ik|x-y|}V(y)f(y)}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dy.$$

Then $K_k$ is compact and $I+K_k$ is boundedly invertible. In particular
$\|(I+K_k)f\|_2\ge\|(I+K_k)^{-1}\|^{-1}\|f\|_2$.
Moreover, on every interval $[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$ the inverses are
operator-norm continuous and uniformly bounded. Writing $K_\zeta$ for the
same kernel with complex wave number $\zeta$, there is $\delta>0$ such that
$I+K_\zeta$ is invertible whenever $\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,[a,b])<\delta$;
its inverses are uniformly bounded there and converge in operator norm to
the outgoing real-axis inverses as $\zeta\to k\in[a,b]$. For incoming
kernels replace $e^{ik|x-y|}$ by $e^{-ik|x-y|}$; the same conclusions hold.
No zero-energy or high-energy uniform bound is claimed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) in dimension $d=3$, let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable
and put $W:=V/c$. For a measurable $U$ let $M_U$ be the maximal
multiplication operator on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with
$D(M_U):=\{f\in L^2:Uf\in L^2\}$ and $M_Uf:=Uf$. Write
$$A_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{4\pi^{2}|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(A_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
$$A:=A_{0}+M_{W},\quad D(A):=D(A_{0}),\qquad H_{0}:=cA_{0},\qquad H:=cA=cA_{0}+M_{V}.$$
$D(A_{0})\subseteq D(M_V)=D(M_W)$ is assumed, and assume that
$A=A_0+M_W$ is self-adjoint on $D(A_0)$. These two hypotheses hold
automatically for real bounded measurable $V$ by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a),(c), so every original bounded-potential case is retained.
So $A_{0}$ is the operator $-\Delta_{w}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
$D(A_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). For a self-adjoint operator $T$ write
$E_{T}$ for the regular projection valued measure of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] and
$\mu^{T}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{T}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in L^{2}$. Then:

(a) $A$ and $H$ are self-adjoint with domain $D(A)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
and $H=cA$ and $H_{0}=cA_{0}$ hold as operator identities on that common domain;

(b) for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B),\qquad E_{H_{0}}(cB)=E_{A_{0}}(B);$$
consequently $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(cB)=\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)$ for every $\psi$ and every
Borel $B$, and $\sigma(H)=c\,\sigma(A)$, $\sigma(H_{0})=c\,\sigma(A_{0})$;

(c) for every $t\in\mathbb R$, with $\tau:=\hbar t/(2m)=\frac{tc}{\hbar}$,
$$e^{-itH/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A},\qquad e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A_{0}},$$
where the exponentials are those of
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]];

(d) let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(L^{2})$ be any family of bounded operators and
$\tau(t):=\hbar t/(2m)$. For every $\psi\in L^{2}$ the strong limit
$\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}F(\tau(t))\psi$ exists if and only if
$\lim_{\tau\to\pm\infty}F(\tau)\psi$ exists, and then the two limits are equal;
in particular
$$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar} =\operatorname*{s-lim}_{\tau\to\pm\infty}e^{i\tau A}e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$$
in the sense that either strong limit exists exactly when the other does, and
then they are equal;

(e) $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure
if and only if $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is, and likewise for singularity with respect
to Lebesgue measure and for absence of atoms; and $\psi\ne0$ is an eigenvector
of $H$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ if and only if it is an eigenvector of $A$
with eigenvalue $\lambda/c$.

The statement is an operator identity and a statement about spectral measures;
no physical interpretation, no scattering limit and no cross section is
asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\hbar>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be
nonempty open sets, and let
$u,v:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ be functions of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) that satisfy the two real
equations
$$\hbar\,\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv,\qquad -\hbar\,\partial_{t}v=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$ for a real-valued function $V$ on $\Omega\times
I$, where $x=(x_0,x_1,x_2)$, $\partial_i$ differentiates in spatial
coordinate $x_i$ for $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ with $t$ fixed,
$\partial_t$ differentiates in $t$ with $x$ fixed, and
$\Delta=\partial_{0}^{2}+\partial_{1}^{2}+\partial_{2}^{2}$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). The equations are the
componentwise reading of
$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi$ for
$\psi:=u+iv$. Put
$$n:=u^{2}+v^{2}:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbf j:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\bigl(u\,\nabla v-v\,\nabla u\bigr):\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^{3},$$
with $\nabla$ the spatial gradient $(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$ of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] at each fixed $t$ and
$\operatorname{div}$ the divergence of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then:

(a) *Continuity identity.* $\partial_{t}n+\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$.

(b) *Stationary solutions.* If $u,v:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are $C^{2}$ and
independent of $t$, if $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is real, and if there is a real
$E$ with
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu=Eu,\qquad -\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv=Ev$$
pointwise on $\Omega$, then $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$ on $\Omega$ for the
time-independent field $\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\nabla v-v\nabla u)$, and for
every closed ball $\overline{B(a,r)}\subseteq\Omega$ with outward unit normal
$\nu$ on the sphere $\partial B(a,r)$,
$$\int_{\partial B(a,r)}\mathbf j\cdot\nu\,dS=0 .$$

(c) *The two explicit readings.* Let $k>0$, $d\in S^{2}$ and define
$u(x):=\cos(kd\cdot x)$, $v(x):=\sin(kd\cdot x)$ on $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$
(then $u,v$ are $C^{\infty}$ and satisfy the stationary equations with $V=0$,
$E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$). Then
$$\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\,d\qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Let $r_{0}>0$, write $\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3}:|x|>r_{0}\}$, let
$\Omega\ni x=r\,\omega$ with $r=|x|$, $\omega\in S^{2}$, and let
$a,b:S^{2}\to\mathbb R$ be functions with $a,b\in C^{1}(S^{2})$. Here
$S^{2}:=\{\omega\in\mathbb R^{3}:|\omega|=1\}$, and, for a function
$g:S^{2}\to\mathbb R$, $g\in C^{1}(S^{2})$ means that its radial extension
$\widetilde g:\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb R$,
$\widetilde g(x):=g(x/|x|)$, is $C^{1}$ in the open-domain sense of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Define
$$u(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\cos(kr)-b(\omega)\sin(kr)}{r},\qquad v(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\sin(kr)+b(\omega)\cos(kr)}{r}$$
on $\Omega$, so that $u+iv=\frac{f(\omega)}{r}e^{ikr}$ with $f:=a+ib$. Then
$u,v\in C^{1}(\Omega)$ and, with $\hat r:=\omega$,
$$\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f(\omega)|^{2}}{r^{2}},\qquad \text{equivalently}\qquad r^{2}\,\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}|f(\omega)|^{2},$$
and the current identity holds for every declared $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$, with no
equation required of the field.

The assertion is an identity for the declared differentiable functions; it
constructs no probability law, no state, no beam and no cross section. The
fields of clause (c) are only $C^{1}$: an $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$ need not admit
two angular derivatives, and no outgoing field is claimed here to solve the
free equation or to be stationary.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), with the short-range
scattering model of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]]: mass $m>0$, spin zero,
state space $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, a declared short-range
potential $V$, the free and interacting assigned energy observables
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and $H$, its reading of the flow by
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Incident plane-wave reading and declared density scale.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **stationary elastic beam
model**. Fix a **wave number** $k>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a **direction**
$d\in S^2$, and an **incident number-density scale** $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. This scale is an explicitly declared model normalization;
no numerical sample density or measured beam value is supplied. Retain the
unit-amplitude, dimensionless incident shape
$$u_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x},$$
with energy reading $E:=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$ in joules. The **physical incident
beam field** is $\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\,u_{\mathrm{inc}}$,
with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$ and constant model number density
$|\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}|^2=n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. For a dimensionless unit-amplitude
shape $\psi$, write $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]:=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$ for the mathematical current of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]. Its incident
value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, with velocity unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The model's
**physical number-current density** is the current of
$\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$,
$$\mathbf j[\Phi]:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline\Phi\nabla\Phi)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi].$$
Thus the **incident current density** and **incident flux density** through a
plane normal to $d$ are
$$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}d,\qquad J_{\mathrm{inc}}:=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}>0,$$
both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)5. The mathematical
plane-wave current of the cited lemma remains the unit-shape computation;
the density factor supplies the declared physical beam normalization.

**(c) Scattered-wave reading and generalized stationary solution.** For a
declared short-range potential $V$ the model declares a **generalized
stationary solution** at energy $E$ and direction $d$ to be a function
$\Psi:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C$ in $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$,
meaning that all weak derivatives of order at most two are locally square
integrable ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), with $V\Psi\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$,
of class $C^{2}$ on the complement of the essential closed support of $V$,
and satisfying the equation on all of $\mathbb R^3$ distributionally:
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Psi(x)\left[-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\eta(x)+(V(x)-E)\eta(x)\right]dx=0\qquad(\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)).$$
Here the essential closed support is the complement of the union of open
sets on which $V=0$ almost everywhere; the test functions are smooth and
compactly supported; $\Delta=\sum_{i=0}^{2}\partial_i^2$ uses the spatial
coordinate convention of the current lemma. Outside the essential closed
support, $V=0$ almost everywhere and $\Psi$ is $C^2$, so the continuous
free-equation residual has zero test pairing and hence vanishes pointwise:
$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\Psi=E\Psi$. The equation containing the declared
representative $V(x)$ holds almost everywhere there; it holds pointwise there
when $V$ is replaced by its zero representative on this exterior open set.
No pointwise equation with arbitrary null-set values of $V$ is asserted.
The solution has the **outgoing asymptotic reading**
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}e^{ikr}+\mathcal E(x),\qquad x=r\Omega,\ r\to\infty,$$
with a **scattering amplitude** function $f_k:S^2\to\mathbb C$, read in
metres relative to the unit incident shape, and a physical beam field

[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]],

existence or uniqueness assertion.

the scattered component, with no assumption that incident/scattered
interference in the total field vanishes.

derivations.claim: Since $V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, so is $W=2mV/\hbar^{2}$, which is read in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$; dividing the physical stationary equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\Psi+V\Psi=E\Psi$ by $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ gives $-\Delta\Psi+W\Psi=(E/c)\Psi$, and $E/c=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)\cdot2m/\hbar^{2}=k^{2}$ by [F3] with $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$.

The kernel $G_{k}(x-y)W(y)$ on $B_{R}\times B_{R}$ is square-integrable because $|x-y|^{-2}$ is locally integrable in three dimensions and $B_{R}$ is bounded, so $K_{k}$ is Hilbert-Schmidt and [F2] gives bounded invertibility of $I+K_{k}$; [F1] then gives $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the distributional equation $(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ and $\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$, which is (a).

By [F1] the smooth amplitude $f_{k}(\Omega)=-(4\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)dy$ and the uniform expansion with the $r^{-2}$ remainder and its tangential and radial derivative bounds hold; these are exactly the displays of (b), with the constant depending on $k,R$ and $\|Wu\|_{1}$.

By [F1] the unit-shape scattered field $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}$ has radial mathematical current $(\hbar k/m)|f_k|^2/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ uniformly. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=u+iv$; the physical field has real and imaginary parts $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u,\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v$. Since the scale is constant, its current is $(\hbar/m)[(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)
abla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)-(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)
abla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}(\hbar/m)(u
abla v-v
abla u)$ by [F4]. Thus the physical scattered current is the display in (c), and the same calculation on the unit incident plane wave gives $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m>0$. Dividing yields $\lim_{r	o\infty}r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}=|f_k|^2$. Smoothness and boundedness of $f_k$ on the sphere, with [F1]'s uniform error, give the finite total cross section $\sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\Omega$. The unit-shape amplitude stays in metres and the density cancels from both cross-section readings. This is (c).

By step 2.1 the constructed $\Psi$ lies in $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and satisfies the global distributional stationary equation after the scaling of [F3]; boundedness of $V$ gives $V\Psi\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$. On the complement of its essential closed support, the convolution integrates the compactly supported $L^1$ density $Wu$ at a positive distance from the kernel singularity locally, so differentiation under the integral gives a smooth field. Here $V=0$ almost everywhere; thus the continuous free-equation residual vanishes distributionally and hence pointwise, as in [F5]. The equation with the declared representative $V$ therefore holds almost everywhere there, and pointwise for its zero exterior representative. Step 3.1 gives the outgoing reading and all required remainder bounds. These facts verify the beam model's generalized stationary solution conditions. The invertible integral problem uniquely fixes the constructed $u$ and hence $\Psi$, which proves the construction-specific uniqueness in (d) and completes the proof.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real, bounded, central (invariant under
rotations) and supported in $B_R$, let $k>0$, and let $f_k\in C^\infty(S^2)$ be
the scattering amplitude of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]].
Then:

(a) $f_k$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its Legendre expansion
$$f_k(\theta)=\frac1{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_l(k)-1\bigr)P_l(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^2(S^2)$ (and absolutely, since $f_k$ is smooth), where
$S_l(k)$ is a unit-modulus number determined by the regular radial solution
$\varphi_l$ normalized by $\varphi_l(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ and by the outgoing
solution $f_l$ with $f_l(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}(1+O(1/r))$: explicitly
$S_l=\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}/W(\varphi_l,f_l)$ and $S_l=e^{2i\delta_l(k)}$
with the phase shift $\delta_l(k)$ defined modulo $\pi$.

(b) $\bigl|\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}\bigr|=\bigl|W(\varphi_l,f_l)\bigr|$, so
$|S_l|=1$, and the total cross section is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_l-1|^2=\frac{4\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^2\delta_l(k),$$
the series converging because $f_k\in L^2(S^2)$ and the expansion in (a) is an
orthogonal expansion.

(c) *Resonance model.* For the single-channel model $S_l(E)=\frac{E-E_r-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_r+i\Gamma/2}$
with $\Gamma>0$ one has $|S_l|=1$ for real $E$ and
$\sin^2\delta_l=\frac{(\Gamma/2)^2}{(E-E_r)^2+(\Gamma/2)^2}$; substituting into
(b) gives the corresponding single-channel cross section. This is a conditional
model calculation, not a theorem that every potential has such a pole.

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, with a **compact-support-class** potential
$V$ supported in the ball $B_{R}$, and adopt the declared stationary elastic
beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave number
$k>0$, direction $d\in S^2$ and the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with incident energy $E=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$.
The construction below retains the dimensionless unit-incident shape
$\Psi$; its physical beam field is $\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$.
Put
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x):=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
for $f\in L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $x\in B_{R}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $I+K_{k}$ is boundedly invertible on $L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$; with
$u:=(I+K_{k})^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}\bigr)$ and
$$\Psi(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)u(y)\,dy,$$
one has $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^{3})$,
$(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ distributionally on $\mathbb R^{3}$, and
$\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$;

(b) with $r=|x|>2R$ and $\Omega=x/r$, the **scattering amplitude**
$$f_{k}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)\,dy$$
is smooth on $S^{2}$ and
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{e^{ikr}f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}+\mathcal E(x),$$
where $|\mathcal E(x)|+|\partial_{r}\mathcal E(x)|\le C(k,R,\|Wu\|_{1})r^{-2}$
uniformly in $\Omega$, and for every fixed product $D_{\Omega}$ of smooth
tangential differential operators on $S^{2}$ also
$|D_{\Omega}\mathcal E|+|D_{\Omega}\partial_{r}\mathcal E|\le C_{D}r^{-2}$;

(c) the physical scattered radial current of the beam model, with
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x})$, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)$$
uniformly in $\Omega$, with physical incident flux density
$J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$;
the common density factor cancels, and the cross-section readings are
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega)=|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}, \qquad \sigma=\int_{S^{2}}|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\Omega<\infty\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}};$$

(d) the solution $\Psi$ of (a) is a generalized stationary solution of the
beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$ in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]], and no other
function satisfying the same equation on the complement of
$\operatorname{supp}V$ and the same outgoing reading is produced by the
construction.

Every assertion is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. The stationary wave is not an element of the state space; the
item asserts no preparation, no beam apparatus, no detector acceptance and no
measured count rate.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** Let $S^2=\{\omega\in\mathbb R^3:|\omega|=1\}$
be the sphere of spatial directions, with polar surface measure $\sigma$
and angle coordinates
$\Phi(\theta,\alpha)=(\sin\theta\cos\alpha,\sin\theta\sin\alpha,\cos\theta)$;

[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] and
$\mu^{T}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{T}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in L^{2}$. Then:

(a) $A$ and $H$ are self-adjoint with domain $D(A)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,

$$\widehat g(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-ip\cdot x}g(x)\,dx,\qquad (F_0g)(E,\omega)=\frac{E^{1/4}}{\sqrt2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\,\omega).$$

and the two stationary transforms by

$$Z_0(E)g=\frac{\sqrt k}{4\pi^{3/2}}\int e^{-ik\omega\cdot x}g(x)\,dx,\qquad Z_\pm(E)g=Z_0(E)\bigl[g-VR_H(E\pm i0)g\bigr].$$

(a) $F_0$ is a unitary from $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ onto
$\mathcal K=L^2((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$. The initially defined stationary
transforms extend to $Z_\pm=F_0\Omega_\pm^*$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$; their
restrictions to $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ are unitary onto $\mathcal K$,
they vanish on the pure point subspace, and they diagonalize $H$ as
multiplication by $E$ on its absolutely continuous subspace.

(b) There is a measurable operator-valued unitary $S(E)$ on $\mathfrak h$
such that $F_0SF_0^*=M_{S(E)}$. No generic nonradial potential is assumed to
preserve individual spherical harmonic channels. For $R\in SO(3)$ set
$V_R(x)=V(R^{-1}x)$ and $(U_Ra)(\omega)=a(R^{-1}\omega)$. The covariance is
$S[V_R](E)=U_RS[V](E)U_R^{-1}$, not commutation with $U_R$ for a fixed
nonradial $V$.

(c) Let $u_{k,d}$ be the outgoing stationary solution restricted to a ball
$B$ containing the support of $V$:

$$u_{k,d}=(I+\chi_BR_0(k^2+i0)V)^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_B\bigr),\qquad f_k(\omega,d)=-\frac1{4\pi}\int_Be^{-ik\omega\cdot x}V(x)u_{k,d}(x)\,dx.$$

Here $R_0(z)=(H_0-z)^{-1}$ and $\chi_B$ denotes restriction/localization;
the inverse is the inverse of **$I+K$**, not of $K$. Define
$(\mathcal A_ka)(\omega)=\int_{S^2}f_k(\omega,d)a(d)\,d\sigma(d)$. Then

$$S(E)=I-2\pi i\,Z_0(E)\bigl[V-VR_H(E+i0)V\bigr]Z_0(E)^*=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_k.$$

Adjoints $Z_0(E)^*$ and products in this formula are understood on the
compact interaction region, not as bounded maps into global $L^2$ plane waves.
The right side is norm-continuous on compact positive-energy intervals and
gives a unitary representative for every $E>0$.

(d) If in addition $V$ is radial, the energy-angular fiber decomposes in the
fixed countable spherical harmonic basis as
$S(E)Y_{lm}=S_l(E)Y_{lm}$. For the reduced radial equation

$$-\varphi_l''+\left(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}+V(r)\right)\varphi_l=k^2\varphi_l,\qquad \varphi_l(r)/r^{l+1}\longrightarrow1,$$

let $f_l$ be the outgoing solution with
$f_l(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}(1+O(r^{-1}))$ outside the interaction region and set
$W_l=W(\varphi_l,f_l)=\varphi_lf_l'-\varphi_l'f_l$. Then

$$S_l(E)=\frac{\overline{W_l(E)}}{W_l(E)},\qquad |S_l(E)|=1.$$

Equivalently, for the real normalized regular solution
$a_l=\sqrt{\rho_l}\,\varphi_l=c_lf_l+d_l\overline f_l$,
$\rho_l=k/(\pi|W_l|^2)$, the multiplier is
$(c_l/d_l)/(c_l^0/d_l^0)$, where the superscript $0$ denotes the corresponding
free normalization. The real regular transforms
$(T_lg)(E)=\int_0^\infty a_l(E,r)g(r)\,dr$ extend to unitaries from the
absolutely continuous reduced radial subspace onto $L^2((0,\infty),dE)$.
They implement the scalar channel statement with the incoming/outgoing phase
factors specified in the proof. No Coulomb continuum transform is used for a
compact potential.

No zero-energy nonresonance, absence of a zero eigenvalue, positivity of the
whole spectrum, finite bound-spectrum assumption, or radiality is imposed on
(a)-(c). The negative and any zero point spectrum are omitted by the
absolutely continuous restriction, rather than falsely declared nonexistent.

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, with a **compact-support-class** potential
$V$ supported in the ball $B_{R}$, and adopt the declared stationary elastic
beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave number
$k>0$, direction $d\in S^2$ and the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with incident energy $E=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$.
The construction below retains the dimensionless unit-incident shape
$\Psi$; its physical beam field is $\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$.
Put
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x):=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
for $f\in L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $x\in B_{R}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $I+K_{k}$ is boundedly invertible on $L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$; with
$u:=(I+K_{k})^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}\bigr)$ and
$$\Psi(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)u(y)\,dy,$$
one has $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^{3})$,
$(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ distributionally on $\mathbb R^{3}$, and
$\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$;

(b) with $r=|x|>2R$ and $\Omega=x/r$, the **scattering amplitude**
$$f_{k}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)\,dy$$
is smooth on $S^{2}$ and
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{e^{ikr}f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}+\mathcal E(x),$$
where $|\mathcal E(x)|+|\partial_{r}\mathcal E(x)|\le C(k,R,\|Wu\|_{1})r^{-2}$
uniformly in $\Omega$, and for every fixed product $D_{\Omega}$ of smooth
tangential differential operators on $S^{2}$ also
$|D_{\Omega}\mathcal E|+|D_{\Omega}\partial_{r}\mathcal E|\le C_{D}r^{-2}$;

(c) the physical scattered radial current of the beam model, with
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x})$, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)$$
uniformly in $\Omega$, with physical incident flux density
$J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$;
the common density factor cancels, and the cross-section readings are
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega)=|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}, \qquad \sigma=\int_{S^{2}}|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\Omega<\infty\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}};$$

(d) the solution $\Psi$ of (a) is a generalized stationary solution of the
beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$ in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]], and no other
function satisfying the same equation on the complement of
$\operatorname{supp}V$ and the same outgoing reading is produced by the
construction.

Every assertion is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. The stationary wave is not an element of the state space; the
item asserts no preparation, no beam apparatus, no detector acceptance and no
measured count rate.

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and a declared **compact-support-class**
potential $V$ supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Let $\Omega_{\pm}$ and $S$ be the
wave operators and scattering operator of clause (d) of that definition,
$E_{H}$ the projection valued measure of the self-adjoint interacting operator
$H$, and $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ its scalar measures. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the wave operators exist by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]], and
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{\pm}\subseteq H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and
$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$, where
$$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ \text{is atomless and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure}\};$$

(b) each wave operator is asymptotically complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H);$$

(c) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the
free flow, $Se^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}S$ for
every $t\in\mathbb R$.

The statement is a conditional consequence of the declared model with a
compactly supported real bounded potential; it asserts no stationary amplitude,
no partial-wave decomposition, no cross section and no measured quantity.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** Let $S^2=\{\omega\in\mathbb R^3:|\omega|=1\}$
be the sphere of spatial directions, with polar surface measure $\sigma$
and angle coordinates
$\Phi(\theta,\alpha)=(\sin\theta\cos\alpha,\sin\theta\sin\alpha,\cos\theta)$;
$d\sigma=\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\alpha$ and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$.
Use exactly the dimensionless spherical harmonics defined in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]:
for integers $l\ge0$ and $0\le q\le l$, set
$$P_l(t)=\frac{1}{2^l l!}\frac{d^l}{dt^l}(t^2-1)^l,\qquad w_{lq}(t)=(-1)^q(1-t^2)^{q/2}\frac{d^q}{dt^q}P_l(t),\qquad b_{lq}=\left(\int_{-1}^1w_{lq}(t)^2\,dt\right)^{-1/2}>0.$$
The continuous representatives $Y_{lq}:S^2\to\mathbb C$ are given by
$$Y_{lq}(\Phi(\theta,\alpha))=\frac{b_{lq}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}w_{lq}(\cos\theta)e^{iq\alpha}\qquad(0<\theta<\pi,\ 0\le\alpha<2\pi),$$
extended continuously to the poles; for $1\le q\le l$ set
$Y_{l,-q}=(-1)^q\overline{Y_{lq}}$. The same symbols denote their
almost-everywhere classes in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$.
Under the declared Countable Choice assumption,
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]] proves that these classes are
orthonormal for $\langle F,G\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline G\,d\sigma$
and their closed linear span is all of $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$.
For a declared central short-range potential $V$, an **angular channel**
$(l,\bar m)$, with integers $l\ge0$ and $-l\le\bar m\le l$, means the
one-dimensional subspace $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{Y_{l\bar m}\}$;
the **partial wave** $l$ means the degree-$l$ sector
$\mathcal H_l:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{Y_{lq}:-l\le q\le l\}$.
The angular indices $q,\bar m$ are distinct from the positive mass $m$.

The radial solutions are those constructed in
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]].
The reduced equation below is read in
physical coordinates after energy division: the reduced potential is
$w:=2mv/\hbar^{2}$ of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] and the energy-divided spectral value is $k^{2}$, both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$,
so that the physical parameters $m,\hbar$ do not enter it explicitly. The
model declares the **regular radial solution**
$\varphi_{l}$ of the reduced equation
$$-\varphi_{l}''+\Bigl(w(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}\Bigr)\varphi_{l}=k^{2}\varphi_{l}, \qquad \varphi_{l}(r)/r^{l+1}\longrightarrow1\quad(r\to0),$$
and the **outgoing radial solution** $f_{l}$ with
$$f_{l}(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}\bigl(1+O(r^{-1})\bigr)\qquad(r\to\infty)$$
outside the interaction region. Both are maps $(0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$
whose functions and first derivatives are locally absolutely continuous;
the reduced equation holds almost everywhere, equivalently in distributions
on $(0,\infty)$, as in the cited theorem's bounded measurable potential
construction. They are not asserted to be elements of the state space.

**(c) Channel factor and phase shift.** The model declares the **channel
factor** and the **phase shift** of the partial wave $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(k):=\frac{\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}}{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}, \qquad S_{l}(k)=e^{2i\delta_{l}(k)},$$
where $W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})=\varphi_{l}f_{l}'-\varphi_{l}'f_{l}$ is the
Wronskian and $\delta_{l}(k)$ is the **phase shift**, a real number read
modulo $\pi$; the model reads $|S_{l}(k)|=1$ and calls the channel
**elastic**. The declared **channel cross-section reading** is
$$\sigma_{l}(k):=\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k),$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The existence of the functions and the identities
$|S_{l}|=1$ and $\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}<\infty$ are proved on this
page and are not presupposed here.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: names
for the objects constructed by the cited mathematics and the reading of the
phase shift modulo $\pi$. The model asserts no identification of the labels
$l,\bar m$ with a measured angular momentum of a material system, no statement
about bound states or their count, and no channel decomposition for
non-central potentials. Every numerical statement about $\delta_{l}$ is a
separate theorem or example of the pair.

derivations.claim: The reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, so [F1] applies to it; by the scaling correspondence the model's operators $H^{\mathrm{free}},H$ are $cA_{0},cA$ with $A_{0}=-\Delta$, $A=-\Delta+M_{W}$ and the physical and energy-divided wave operators coincide.

By [F2] the model's stationary amplitude for direction $d$ is the amplitude of [F1]'s stationary problem for $W$ at the same wave number $k$; hence $\mathcal A_{k}$ is exactly the on-shell amplitude operator of [F1].

By [F1] the free trace transform $F_{0}$ diagonalizes the free flow and $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ with $S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k}$; since the model's $S$ and $\mathcal A_{k}$ are the same operators as in [F1] by steps 1.1 and 2.1, the displays of (a) and (b) follow, including unitarity of the on-shell operator.

By [F1] the covariance identity $S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}S[V](E)U_{R}^{-1}$ holds for the energy-divided potential; since rotations act on $W$ exactly as on $V$ through $R^{-1}$, the same identity is the model's (c).

If $V$ is central, so is $W$; [F1], with its integer harmonic index renamed $\bar m$ as in [F3], gives $S(E)Y_{l\bar m}=S_{l}(k)Y_{l\bar m}$ with $S_{l}=\overline{W_{l}}/W_{l}$; by [F3] the model's channel vocabulary names exactly these objects $S_{l}=\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$ and $\delta_{l}$, and the phase-shift series of the partial-wave theorem is the total cross-section reading of this decomposition. This is (d) and completes the proof.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\gamma>0$, $H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_\gamma:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(H_\gamma)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, the
self-adjoint Coulomb operator established below on this exact domain, with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$ as proved by the local compact-resolvent argument. Use the physical-momentum Fourier transform $\mathcal F_pf(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\mathcal F_2f(p/(2\pi))$, unitary by the dilation change of variables, equivalently $(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)dx$ on Schwartz functions. Let $P_j=\mathcal F_p^*M_{p_j}\mathcal F_p=-i\partial_j$ on its maximal weak-derivative domain; thus $H_0=\mathcal F_p^*M_{|p|^2}\mathcal F_p$. Set $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$ for $p\ne0$ and $a(0)=0$, and $a(P)=\mathcal F_p^*M_a\mathcal F_p$ on the maximal multiplier domain. For $|t|\ge1$ define the
Dollard-modified free evolution
$$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}e^{i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\,a(P)\log|t|}$$
(the two factors commute, being functions of $P$; extend to $|t|\le1$ by
$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}$). Then:

(a) $U_D(t)$ is unitary for every $t$ and strongly continuous in $t$ away from $t=0$; on the dense set of momentum $C_c^\infty$ vectors supported in an annulus $0<a_0\le|p|\le b_0<\infty$ it is differentiable for $|t|>1$, with the exterior one-sided derivatives at $t=\pm1$, and
$$i\,U_D'(t)=\Bigl[H_0-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\qquad(|t|>1).$$

(b) *Integrable remainder.* For every vector $\psi$ in that dense set one has
$$\int_1^\infty\Bigl\|\Bigl[\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\psi\Bigr\|_2dt<\infty,$$
and the same integral with $|t|$ in the comparison denominator over $(-\infty,-1]$ is finite. More precisely, for each such $\psi$ there are $T_\psi\ge1$ and $C_\psi<\infty$ such that for both signs of $t$, $|t|\ge T_\psi$ implies $\|[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|t|\,|P|)]U_D(t)\psi\|_2\le C_\psi(1+\log|t|)/|t|^2$.

No empirical claim, no Rutherford cross-section and no photon interpretation is
asserted; the logarithmic phase is a comparison construction for the
long-range generator.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$,
$H_0=-\Delta$, $H_\gamma=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and let
$U_D(t)$ be the Dollard-modified evolution of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]], with modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_\gamma}U_D(t)$, whose existence on all of $L^2$ is included in the claimed conclusion. Then:

(a) $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH_\gamma}\Omega_{D\pm}$ for all $s$;

(b) *Per-channel form.* With the Coulomb angular-radial unitary
$\widehat T_{\gamma,l}$ and its free analogue $\widehat T_{0,l}$ constructed
below with regular coefficient one and density $\sqrt E/(\pi|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2)$, the operator $\Omega_{D\pm}$ acts in
each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function $b_{l,\pm}(E)$
of the energy;

(c) *Completeness.* $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, hence
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\gamma)=H_{\mathrm{c}}(H_\gamma)$
and the modified scattering operator $S_D=\Omega_{D+}^*\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$.

The statement covers the exactly Coulombic two-body model with $\gamma>0$; it
does not assert explicit scattering amplitudes or measured cross sections.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space, let $H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E$ be a projection valued measure on
$(X,\Sigma)$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and $\Sigma$-measurable
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). Then:

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$
3. the exact norm is the **$E$-essential supremum**
$$\|f\|_{E,\infty}:=\sup\bigl\{\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}:\ x\in H,\ \|x\|=1\bigr\}, \qquad \|\Phi_E(f)\|=\|f\|_{E,\infty},$$
   where $\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}$ denotes the essential supremum of the real measurable function $|f|$ with respect to
   the finite measure $E_x$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator with spectral
projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ acting on a complex Hilbert space $H$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let
$f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be Borel. Write $u(T)=u(E)$, with the truncation definition below. If $H=\{0\}$, use its unique PVM and unique full-domain operator directly. Then:

1. $f(T)^*=\overline f(T)$;
2. $f(T)g(T)$ has domain $D(g(T))\cap D((fg)(T))$ and equals the restriction of
   $(fg)(T)$ to that domain, and its closure is $(fg)(T)$;
3. on $D(f(T))\cap D(g(T))$ the sum $f(T)+g(T)$ equals the restriction of
   $(f+g)(T)$, and the closure of $f(T)+g(T)$ is $(f+g)(T)$;
4. the spectrum of $f(T)$ is the essential range
   $\{z\in\mathbb C:E(f^{-1}(B_\varepsilon(z)))\ne0$ for every
   $\varepsilon>0\}$ of $f$ with respect to $E$;
5. if $f$ is continuous then that essential range is the closure of
   $f(\sigma(T))$, with the closure redundant when $f(\sigma(T))$ is closed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a
densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $c>0$ be
real. Write $cA$ for the operator with domain $D(cA):=D(A)$ and
$(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$. Then:

(a) $cA$ is self-adjoint.

(b) For every $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $z\in\rho(cA)$ if and only if
$z/c\in\rho(A)$, and then
$(cA-z)^{-1}=c^{-1}(A-z/c)^{-1}$; consequently
$\rho(cA)=c\,\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(cA)=c\,\sigma(A)$.

(c) If some, hence every, resolvent of $A$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]), then every resolvent of $cA$ is compact and
$A$ and $cA$ have the same complete orthonormal eigenfamily $(e_j)_{j\in J}$.
If $N:=\dim H<\infty$, take $J=\{1,\ldots,N\}$; if $H$ is infinite dimensional,
take $J=\mathbb N$, with $|\mu_j|\to\infty$ and each eigenvalue repeated
according to its finite multiplicity. In both cases $Ae_j=\mu_je_j$,
$(cA)e_j=c\mu_je_j$, and
$$\sigma(A)=\{\mu_j:j\in J\},\qquad\sigma(cA)=\{c\mu_j:j\in J\}$$
with no other spectral points. The finite-dimensional conclusion also holds
without a separate compactness assumption, since bounded operators on such
$H$ are compact.

(d) Eigenvectors correspond exactly: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in H$,
$x\ne0$, one has $x\in D(A)$ and $Ax=\lambda x$ if and only if
$x\in D(cA)$ and $(cA)x=(c\lambda)x$; and every eigenvalue of $cA$ has the same
eigenspace as the corresponding eigenvalue of $A$.

(e) If $A\ge\gamma$ in the quadratic-form sense, meaning that
$\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge\gamma\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, then
$cA\ge c\gamma$ in the same sense.

Only the scaling of the given operator is asserted; no domain, spectrum or
eigenvector is claimed for any other rescaling, and no physical
interpretation is attached.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],

constant $\hbar>0$ and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared Coulomb model.** As an additional model assumption of the
pair, fix a **coupling** $\kappa>0$, read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$, and adopt the
**one-centre Coulomb model** of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] in its spin-zero
one-particle reading: the declared potential is
$$V_{\kappa}(x):=-\frac{\kappa}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),$$
read in joules, with the value at the origin a declared convention that does
not affect the theory, and the **assigned energy observable** is
$$H_{\kappa}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}-\frac{\kappa}{|\cdot|}$$
on the domain $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
self-adjoint there by
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] clause (a) with flow
$e^{-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]. The model declares the
free comparison operator to be the free assigned energy observable
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (c), and reads its
Coulomb coupling in the inverse-length form
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\quad(\mathrm{m^{-1}}), \qquad\text{so that}\qquad H_{\kappa}=c\Bigl(-\Delta_{w}-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\Bigr),\quad c=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}.$$
The pure Coulomb potential is **not** in the short-range classes of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b); it is the
model's long-range case.

**(c) The declared Dollard-modified comparison.** Choose a reference length $\ell_\star>0$, read in metres, as a comparison convention, and put
$$t_{\star}:=\frac{2m\ell_\star^2}{\hbar}\quad(\mathrm{s}).$$
and, for $t\ne0$, let $h_{t}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be the bounded Borel
function
$$h_{t}(x):=\exp\Bigl(i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\, \frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mx}}\,\log\frac{|t|}{t_{\star}}\Bigr)\quad(x>0), \qquad h_{t}(0):=1 .$$
The model declares the **Dollard-modified free comparison** to be the family
$$U_{D}(t):=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\,h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})\quad(t\ne0), \qquad U_{D}(0):=I,$$
where $h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ is the bounded functional calculus
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 1) of the self-adjoint free
operator: since $h_{t}$ is unimodular, $U_{D}(t)$ is unitary for every $t$,
and both factors are functions of $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and commute. The
**modified wave operators** of the model are the strong limits
$$\Omega_{D\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}U_{D}(t),$$
declared when both exist, and the **modified scattering operator** is
$S_{D}:=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ when both exist and are isometries. The
reference length and the resulting time $t_\star$ are declared conventions. More exactly, changing the reference time from $t_\star$ to $t_\star'$ multiplies $U_D(t)$ on the right, for each sign $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, by the fixed free-energy unitary
$$Q_\sigma= q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}}),\qquad q_\sigma(E)=\exp\Bigl(-i\sigma\frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mE}}\log\frac{t_\star'}{t_\star}\Bigr)\quad(E>0),\qquad q_\sigma(0)=1.$$
It is a bounded unimodular Borel multiplier and commutes with the free flow. Hence, when the wave operators exist, $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. The completeness and isometry properties are unchanged; these are the fixed outgoing and incoming phase conventions.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: a
prescribed long-range potential with its assigned energy observable, and a
modified comparison construction for it. The model asserts no formula for a
Coulomb scattering amplitude, no Rutherford cross section and no measured
quantity; the modification is a comparison construction for the long-range
generator, not a new interaction or a measured force. The ordinary
short-range comparison of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (d) is not claimed
to be complete for the Coulomb model; its completeness is established only
for the modified comparison, on this page.

operator $H_{\kappa}$ on $D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
assigned sharp-observable reading
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the flow and
preparation reading [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and

[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],

(a) $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model:
$H_{\kappa}$ is densely defined, self-adjoint and bounded below on
$D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, acts by
$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa f/|\cdot|$, and
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H_{\kappa})=[0,+\infty);$$
every point of $\sigma(H_{\kappa})\cap(-\infty,0)$ is an eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity, isolated in $\sigma(H_{\kappa})$, and the set of negative eigenvalues is
at most countable;

(b) *Flow.* The family $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is the model's
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation
$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\kappa}\psi(t)$ holds in the norm-differentiable
sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$, and for other
vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not asserted; density
preparations evolve by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with $\rho(t)$ a density
operator for every $t$;

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{0}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure preparation
$[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and only if
$\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$; in that case, with eigenvalue $E$,
one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ for a normalised $\psi$, and every bounded assigned sharp
observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in
this preparation;

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit vector $\psi$ the position outcome law is
$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$; if $\psi$ is in addition a unit
eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$ with eigenvalue $E$, then the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ are readings of the same
preparation through the declared observables, with no joint-measurement claim;

(e) *Spectral support and exact values.* For every preparation $\rho$ one has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\sigma(H_{\kappa}))=1$, and an exact energy value
$\lambda$ has $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an
eigenvalue, in which case the probability is the total weight of the
eigenspace; in particular no exact value in $\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(H_{\kappa})$
is admissible, and the item asserts neither that $0$ is an eigenvalue nor any
statement about eigenvalues in the positive half-line, which are excluded by
the following radial items;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. It asserts no eigenvalue list, no
degeneracy, no transition, radiation or line-intensity statement, no
identification of $\kappa$, $m$ or $\hbar$ with measured constants, and no
empirical result.

derivations.claim: [Numerical SI comparison with dimensionless arguments] Write the fixed SI units as $L_0=1\,\mathrm m$, $T_0=1\,\mathrm s$, $M_0=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$. Let $m_0=m/M_0$, $h_0=\hbar/(E_0T_0)$, $k_0=\kappa/(E_0L_0)$, $L=\ell_\star/L_0>0$ and $t_0=t/T_0$ be their numerical values, and put $\gamma_0=\gamma L_0=2m_0k_0/h_0^2$, $c_0=h_0^2/(2m_0)$ and $\tau=h_0t_0/(2m_0)$. These are pure real numbers, with $\tau\to\pm\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$. Represent the wavefunctions in the numerical SI coordinate $q=x/L_0$, with the normalized $L^2$ coordinate map $\mathcal J_0f(q)=L_0^{3/2}f(L_0q)$, the Jacobian normalization understood in the chosen length unit. Substitution in the integral proves this map unitary; weak derivative substitution gives its exact $H^2$ domain transport. The numerical energy representatives are therefore $\mathsf H_\kappa=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H_\kappa\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0C_{\gamma_0}$ and $\mathsf H_f=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H^{\mathrm{free}}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0A_0$, where $A_0=-\Delta_q$ and $C_{\gamma_0}=-\Delta_q-\gamma_0/|q|$. Thus $\mathcal J_0e^{-itH_\kappa/\hbar}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}$ and similarly for the free operator. The numerical reference time is $t_{\star,0}=2m_0L^2/h_0$, so $\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\frac{|t_0|}{t_{\star,0}}=\frac{|\tau|}{L^2},\qquad \log\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\log|\tau|-2\log L.$ Every logarithm has a dimensionless argument; no time having units of length squared is placed inside the source logarithm.

[Exact fixed energy phases] For a positive numerical energy $e=c_0\lambda$, the phase coefficient of the physical definition is $m_0k_0/(h_0\sqrt{2m_0e})=\gamma_0/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. By [F1], $a(P)=\gamma_0/(2|P|)$ for the numerical source $A_0=|P|^2$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ define the fixed bounded unitary $B_{\sigma,L}=b_{\sigma,L}(A_0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(\lambda)=\exp\Bigl(-2i\sigma\frac{\gamma_0}{2\sqrt\lambda}\log L\Bigr)\quad(\lambda>0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(0)=1.$ The functions are bounded unimodular Borel functions despite their oscillation near zero, so their calculus is defined on all $L^2$ and they commute with $e^{-irA_0}$ for every $r$. Spectral correspondence [F3] and step 1.1 give, for $|\tau|\ge1$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\mathcal J_0U_D(t)\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau A_0}e^{i\sigma a(P)\log|\tau|}B_{\sigma,L}=U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\sigma,L}.$ The bounded functional calculus also transports under $\mathcal J_0$: conjugating the PVM gives a regular PVM representing the numerical operator, so spectral uniqueness identifies it and simple-function approximation gives the claimed calculus transport. If desired, the annular smooth momentum class in [F1] is preserved by each $B_{\sigma,L}$ because its multiplier is smooth on every compact annulus; hence the source remainder estimate remains integrable on that class after this fixed phase. The comparison for finite $|\tau|<1$ need not equal the source's short-time extension and is irrelevant to the two asymptotic limits.

[Strong limits, isometry and intertwining] Apply [F2] at the positive numerical coupling $\gamma_0$. Let $W_\pm$ be its two full-space Dollard wave operators. Step 2.1 makes the physical comparison product, conjugated by $\mathcal J_0$, equal $e^{i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\pm,L}$ on the corresponding exterior half-line. The fixed bounded right factor and the positive scalar time change let the strong limits pass on every vector, giving $\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}W_\pm B_{\pm,L}\mathcal J_0.$ Both $W_\pm$ are isometries by [F2] and both $B_{\pm,L}$ are unitaries, so these operators are isometries. For physical $s\in\mathbb R$, put $r=h_0(s/T_0)/(2m_0)$. The numerical free/Coulomb flows are $e^{-irA_0}$ and $e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$ by step 1.1. Since $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with the free flow and $W_\pm e^{-irA_0}=e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_\pm$, conjugating gives the exact intertwining of (a). No new source existence or momentum-domain assumption was introduced.

[Full completeness under the reference convention] Because $B_{\pm,L}$ are onto, step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}\operatorname{ran}W_\pm$. By [F2], this is $\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm{ac}}(C_{\gamma_0})=\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm c}(C_{\gamma_0})$. Positive energy scaling by $c_0$ preserves these spectral subspaces [F3], and the unitary numerical coordinate representation transports the spectral measures and their subspaces as in step 2.1. The resulting physical subspaces are exactly $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\kappa)=H_{\mathrm c}(H_\kappa)$. This proves (b) for every declared reference length, preserving the source's whole continuous subspace and all angular channels.

[Scattering phases, unitarity and free-flow commutation] Put $S^{\mathrm{nd}}=W_+^*W_-$. The formula in step 3.1 gives $S_D=\mathcal J_0^{-1}B_{+,L}^*S^{\mathrm{nd}}B_{-,L}\mathcal J_0.$ All factors are unitary by [F2] and step 2.1, so $S_D$ is unitary. The commutation with the free flow follows directly from the two intertwinings: taking the adjoint of the plus identity at time $-r$ gives $e^{-irA_0}W_+^*=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$, hence $S^{\mathrm{nd}}e^{-irA_0}=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_-=e^{-irA_0}S^{\mathrm{nd}}$. The fixed $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with that same flow, so their scattering product does too, and conjugating proves (c). Equivalently the common range projection from step 4.1 gives both $S_D^*S_D=I$ and $S_DS_D^*=I$. For any other reference time $t_\star'$, let $Q_\sigma=q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ with $q_\sigma(E)=\exp(-i\sigma\alpha(E)\log(t_\star'/t_\star))$, $\alpha(E)=m\kappa/(\hbar\sqrt{2mE})$ for $E>0$ and $q_\sigma(0)=1$. The defining phases give exactly $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. These incoming/outgoing factors are different sign conventions, not a claim that the scattering operator itself is unchanged.

[Scope and assembly] Steps 3.1–5.1 establish all the original modified-limit, isometry, intertwining, full completeness and scattering-unitarity conclusions with their corrected dimensional convention. No step supplies the ordinary unmodified Coulomb wave limits, so (d) retains exactly that distinction. The reference length adds only a comparison convention and its fixed channel phases; it adds no hypothesis on a state or on the Coulomb interaction, no amplitude formula and no measured cross section.

citations.quote:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, and its partial-wave and phase-shift
reading [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] for a
declared central short-range potential. Fix a **partial-wave label**
$l\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ in the sense of clause (b) of that reading.
Here a single channel means the whole degree-$l$ partial-wave sector:
$\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l\mu}:-l\le\mu\le l,\ \mu\in\mathbb Z\}$,
with all $2l+1$ angular labels $(l,\mu)$ sharing the same scalar factor
$S_l$. The symbol $\mu$ is the angular index; $m$ remains the positive mass.
This convention agrees with that reading's $\sigma_l$, which includes
all these angular labels. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) The declared single-channel resonance model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix real **resonance parameters** $E_{r}$ and
$\Gamma>0$, both read in joules, and **declare** the channel factor of the
label $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(E):=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}\qquad(E>0),$$
read for positive energies only, with the **phase shift** of the channel read
from the relation $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ modulo $\pi$ and the **channel
cross-section reading**
$$\sigma_{l}(E):=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E), \qquad k(E):=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The model calls $E_{r}$ the **resonance energy** and
$\Gamma$ the **width parameter**; both are declared model parameters and
neither is identified with a measured quantity. The parameter $E_r$ may be
zero or negative; calling it a resonance energy does not assign a physical
cross section at that parameter value unless $E_r>0$. Auxiliary real-axis
algebraic comparisons of the Lorentzian factor do not extend $k(E)$ or
$\sigma_l(E)$ beyond the positive-energy domain.

**(c) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(b) declare a conditional one-channel
model. The pair asserts no analytic continuation, no pole of the resolvent and
no property of any potential that would produce the declared factor
$S_{l}$; the model is used only to compute the induced phase shift and channel
cross section of the declared factor. In particular, no exponential decay law,
no lifetime $\hbar/\Gamma$ and no Lorentzian line shape of a measured
distribution is asserted or derived; those would be separate models with their
own assumptions and their own uncertainty qualifications.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real, bounded, central (invariant under
rotations) and supported in $B_R$, let $k>0$, and let $f_k\in C^\infty(S^2)$ be
the scattering amplitude of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]].
Then:

(a) $f_k$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its Legendre expansion
$$f_k(\theta)=\frac1{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_l(k)-1\bigr)P_l(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^2(S^2)$ (and absolutely, since $f_k$ is smooth), where
$S_l(k)$ is a unit-modulus number determined by the regular radial solution
$\varphi_l$ normalized by $\varphi_l(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ and by the outgoing
solution $f_l$ with $f_l(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}(1+O(1/r))$: explicitly
$S_l=\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}/W(\varphi_l,f_l)$ and $S_l=e^{2i\delta_l(k)}$
with the phase shift $\delta_l(k)$ defined modulo $\pi$.

(b) $\bigl|\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}\bigr|=\bigl|W(\varphi_l,f_l)\bigr|$, so
$|S_l|=1$, and the total cross section is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_l-1|^2=\frac{4\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^2\delta_l(k),$$
the series converging because $f_k\in L^2(S^2)$ and the expansion in (a) is an
orthogonal expansion.

(c) *Resonance model.* For the single-channel model $S_l(E)=\frac{E-E_r-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_r+i\Gamma/2}$
with $\Gamma>0$ one has $|S_l|=1$ for real $E$ and
$\sin^2\delta_l=\frac{(\Gamma/2)^2}{(E-E_r)^2+(\Gamma/2)^2}$; substituting into
(b) gives the corresponding single-channel cross section. This is a conditional
model calculation, not a theorem that every potential has such a pole.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** Let $S^2=\{\omega\in\mathbb R^3:|\omega|=1\}$
be the sphere of spatial directions, with polar surface measure $\sigma$
and angle coordinates
$\Phi(\theta,\alpha)=(\sin\theta\cos\alpha,\sin\theta\sin\alpha,\cos\theta)$;
$d\sigma=\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\alpha$ and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$.
Use exactly the dimensionless spherical harmonics defined in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]:
for integers $l\ge0$ and $0\le q\le l$, set
$$P_l(t)=\frac{1}{2^l l!}\frac{d^l}{dt^l}(t^2-1)^l,\qquad w_{lq}(t)=(-1)^q(1-t^2)^{q/2}\frac{d^q}{dt^q}P_l(t),\qquad b_{lq}=\left(\int_{-1}^1w_{lq}(t)^2\,dt\right)^{-1/2}>0.$$
The continuous representatives $Y_{lq}:S^2\to\mathbb C$ are given by
$$Y_{lq}(\Phi(\theta,\alpha))=\frac{b_{lq}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}w_{lq}(\cos\theta)e^{iq\alpha}\qquad(0<\theta<\pi,\ 0\le\alpha<2\pi),$$
extended continuously to the poles; for $1\le q\le l$ set
$Y_{l,-q}=(-1)^q\overline{Y_{lq}}$. The same symbols denote their
almost-everywhere classes in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$.
Under the declared Countable Choice assumption,
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]] proves that these classes are
orthonormal for $\langle F,G\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline G\,d\sigma$
and their closed linear span is all of $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$.
For a declared central short-range potential $V$, an **angular channel**
$(l,\bar m)$, with integers $l\ge0$ and $-l\le\bar m\le l$, means the
one-dimensional subspace $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{Y_{l\bar m}\}$;
the **partial wave** $l$ means the degree-$l$ sector
$\mathcal H_l:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{Y_{lq}:-l\le q\le l\}$.
The angular indices $q,\bar m$ are distinct from the positive mass $m$.

The radial solutions are those constructed in
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]].
The reduced equation below is read in
physical coordinates after energy division: the reduced potential is
$w:=2mv/\hbar^{2}$ of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] and the energy-divided spectral value is $k^{2}$, both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$,
so that the physical parameters $m,\hbar$ do not enter it explicitly. The
model declares the **regular radial solution**
$\varphi_{l}$ of the reduced equation

derivations.claim: For any real $E$, write $x:=E-E_r$ and $y:=\Gamma/2>0$. Then $x+iy\ne0$ and the purely algebraic ratio $R(E):=(x-iy)/(x+iy)$ has modulus one because its numerator is the conjugate of its denominator. On the physical range $E>0$, [F1] identifies $R(E)=S_l(E)$, proving the first part of (a). Defining $R$ as an auxiliary real-axis rational formula does not assign $k$ or a physical cross section outside the range $E>0$.

With $r:=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}>0$ and $\theta:=\operatorname{Arg}(x+iy)\in(0,\pi)$, one has $x+iy=r e^{i\theta}$ and $x-iy=r e^{-i\theta}$, hence $R(E)=e^{-2i\theta}$. For $E>0$ the phase $\delta_l=-\theta$ modulo $\pi$ therefore matches [F1]. When $x\ne0$, $\tan\theta=y/x$ and the principal arctangent gives the same angle modulo $\pi$; when $x=0$, $\theta=\pi/2$, so the phase is $-\pi/2$ with no division by zero. This proves all of (a).

For $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l=\sin^2\theta=y^2/(x^2+y^2)=L(E)$, in agreement with [F2]. Independently, the real-axis formula has positive denominator for every real $E$ and satisfies $0<L(E)\le1$, with equality $L(E)=1$ exactly when $x=0$. Also $L(E)=1/2$ if and only if $x^2=y^2$, so its two real half-height points are $E_r-y$ and $E_r+y$, separated by $2y=\Gamma$. Restricting a point to the physical range requires that point to be positive; the mathematical peak and width identities impose no condition such as $E_r>y$. This proves (b).

For $E>0$, substituting step 3.1 into [F1], [F3] gives $\sigma_l(E)=4\pi(2l+1)L(E)/k(E)^2$. If $E_r>0$, this formula is defined at $E=E_r$, where $L(E_r)=1$ and $k(E_r)^2=2mE_r/\hbar^2$, yielding the displayed resonance-centre value. If $E_r\le0$, no such physical evaluation is in the model's domain and the auxiliary $L(E_r)=1$ does not create one. The extra factor $k(E)^{-2}$ remains energy dependent, so no location-of-maximum or slow-variation assertion is used. This proves (c), retaining every real $E_r$ and positive $\Gamma$.

Use exactly the dimensionless spherical harmonics defined in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]:
for integers $l\ge0$ and $0\le q\le l$, set
$$P_l(t)=\frac{1}{2^l l!}\frac{d^l}{dt^l}(t^2-1)^l,\qquad w_{lq}(t)=(-1)^q(1-t^2)^{q/2}\frac{d^q}{dt^q}P_l(t),\qquad b_{lq}=\left(\int_{-1}^1w_{lq}(t)^2\,dt\right)^{-1/2}>0.$$

almost-everywhere classes in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$.

orthonormal for $\langle F,G\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline G\,d\sigma$

$\mathcal H_l:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{Y_{lq}:-l\le q\le l\}$.

[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]].
